root.name: Ruy Lopez: Open Berlin Defense, l'Hermet Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 Nf6 4. O-O Nxe4 5. d4 Nd6 6. dxe5

overview: After 6.dxe5 Black takes the bishop with ...Nxb5 7.a4 Nbd4 8.Nxd4 Nxd4 9.Qxd4 d5 10.exd6 Qxd6, leading to open play with accurate defence. Black's pieces are active but White has a slight edge; the line is theory-heavy but less played than the Showalter.

white_ideas.idea: Win the bishop pair or a lead in development
Break with a4 to harass the knight
Trade queens and play for a small endgame edge

black_ideas.idea: Use active pieces and a central pawn
Trade down to a safe endgame

typical_structures.structure: Open position with isolated e5 or queenless

character.notes: Open play where both sides must know their moves but Black is solid.

sublines_that_differ.name: Showalter Variation
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 Nf6 4. O-O Nxe4 5. d4 Nd6 6. Ba4
sublines_that_differ.how: White retreats the bishop; a different, more flexible line.

character.reason: Black's Berlin set-up is resilient and queens tend to come off.

gambit.reason: Material is level and any pawn comes back by force.

structure.reason: Central pawns have been exchanged, leaving open lines.

level.reason: Some theory is needed but not extreme.
